chain.label: Crew-fueler miscommunication: only 90 gal loaded instead of intended 180 gal
chain.trigger: The larger pilot told him to put 45 gallons in the other tank for a total of 90 gallons

chain.label: Flight crew did not verify the fuel actually loaded or ensure an adequate fuel supply
chain.trigger: the fueler stated that he 'did not observe either pilot check the fuel drip sticks, climb up the fueler's ladder to check the fuel, or walk around the airplane'

chain.label: Low fuel quantity annunciator lights not designed as warnings and easily obscured/overlooked
chain.trigger: the low fuel quantity annunciator lights were not designed to be warning lights... at certain seat positions, a portion of the control wheel blocked a clear view of these lights

chain.label: Mountainous ridgeline terrain south of AVP at 1,755 ft msl beneath the flightpath
chain.trigger: the controller informed the pilots... that there was a ridgeline between them and the airport

chain.label: IMC approach to near minimums forced a missed approach and a lengthy second approach, increasing fuel burn
chain.trigger: a previous landing...aircraft picked up the airport at minimums; the airplane... began to climb again... when a missed approach was executed

chain.label: Airplane departed with ~800 lb less fuel than manifested and reached a critically low/exhausted fuel state
chain.trigger: the accident airplane departed FRG with about 1,600 pounds of fuel on board, which is 800 pounds less than listed on the load manifest

caused_by.evidence: a lack of clear communication between the pilots and the fueler resulted in only 90 gallons (about 600 pounds) of fuel being added
the flight crew's failure to ensure an adequate fuel supply, the airplane departed FRG with less fuel than the flight crewmembers stated on the load manifest
Fuel burn is also increased during rapid, high-performance climbs, such as required for the execution of a missed approach

chain.label: Crew failed to monitor fuel gauges and remained unaware of the low fuel state
chain.trigger: the flight crewmembers failed to adequately monitor the airplane's fuel state en route and at ACY based on the expectation that they had sufficient fuel

caused_by.evidence: the pilots discounted the accuracy of the fuel gauges in flight because they had measured the tanks and believed that they added sufficient fuel (180 gallons)
Safety Board investigators determined in simulations that these annunciator lights were easily overlooked, even when illuminated

chain.label: Right engine stopped during the second ILS approach; emergency declared
chain.trigger: the approach controller asked the nature of the problem, and the captain responded, 'engine failure'

caused_by.evidence: given the larger amount of fuel loaded in the left fuel tank, the right engine stoppage could be explained by fuel exhaustion

chain.label: Asymmetric thrust left uncorrected: 55° right deviation off the localizer and sustained sideslip
chain.trigger: the accident airplane deviated 55° in a right turn away from the localizer course during the second approach

caused_by.evidence: The deviation to the right was likely the result of asymmetrical thrust caused by stoppage of the right engine
caused them to be less vigilant in their monitoring of the airplane's fuel state and slower to consider a low fuel state as the cause of the initial engine failure

chain.label: Maneuvering/sideslip unported the small remaining left tank fuel, causing repeated left engine stoppage and restart
chain.trigger: the flight crew's maneuvering after the right engine stoppage may have intermittently unported it, causing the sequential stoppage and restarting of the left engine

caused_by.evidence: the apparent difficulties with the left engine could be explained by unporting of whatever fuel remained in the left tank
Conditions would have been conducive to unporting if... the airplane was in a left bank and in a nose-right sideslip following the loss of the right engine

chain.label: Loss of control at low altitude and reduced airspeed (103 knots) with intermittent left engine power
chain.trigger: the final loss of control may have been precipitated by momentary stopping or starting of the left engine when the airplane was at a reduced airspeed

caused_by.evidence: the airplane was more difficult to control and required constant flight control and trim inputs when the left engine was intermittently failed and restored
Impact witness marks and airplane damage were consistent with a loss of control at low altitude

chain.label: Steep, high-bank impact with mountain terrain and postcrash fire
chain.trigger: the airplane impacted the ground at a 60° nose low attitude and in a 135° left bank

caused_by.evidence: Impact witness marks and airplane damage were consistent with a loss of control at low altitude
The airplane wreckage was found on the top of a mountain on the east side of a pipeline clearway

chain.label: All 19 occupants fatally injured by blunt force trauma
chain.trigger: 17 passengers and two flight crewmembers were killed

caused_by.evidence: The accident was not survivable because of high impact forces. Autopsies determined that the passengers and flight crew died of blunt force trauma
